tools.name: wrap_up
tools.description: Close a turn in which you did work (edited files, ran commands) with a short wrap-up box the operator sees under your answer. Call it once, as the last thing you do in such a turn; skip it for a turn that only answered a question. `recap`: one or two plain sentences on what changed and where things stand. `ask`: only when you need the operator to decide or answer something before you go on. `next`: at most two next steps you recommend, the best one first, each written as the exact instruction the operator would send you ("Commit these changes", "Run the full test suite"); leave it out when there is no obvious next step.

recap.description: One or two sentences: what changed and where things stand.

ask.description: The question you need answered before going on, if any.

blocked.description: True when you cannot go on until the operator answers or acts.

next.description: Up to two next steps, best first, each the exact instruction to send you.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description:
The operator follows your progress on the plan Ferrite shows under your latest message, not by reading your messages, so keeping it is part of doing the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets a plan; only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not. Make it with `update_plan` in the same message as the turn's very first tool call, even one that only reads or lists files: the whole plan in order, 2-7 short imperative steps of a few words each ("Read the parser", "Fix the off-by-one", "Run the tests"), the step you are starting in progress and the rest pending. If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the plan once you know. Never spend a message on `update_plan` alone. As each step finishes, mark it completed and the next one in progress, in the same message as the call that starts that next step; work you do in parallel still moves the plan as it lands. Keep exactly one step in progress while you work. Before your closing answer, the plan must say what you did: no step you finished is left in progress or pending. When the operator steers you or the scope changes, send the new whole plan, so it never shows an abandoned one. Do not also write the plan as a list in your message.

- First call: `scope` and `items` (each step `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed`). `scope` says what the request is to this conversation: `first_task` until you have finished a task here; then `new_task` for unrelated work, or `continuation` for everything else (the next iteration, acting on what you just found or suggested; when unsure, this one).
- Next step: `{"advance": true}` alongside the call that begins it: it completes the step in progress and starts the next pending one. After the last step, advance alongside `wrap_up` (a `wrap_up` that is not blocked also checks off what is left).
- Out of order: `{"done": [2], "start": 4}` (1-based step numbers).
- Plan changed: `items` again, the new whole plan.
The answer says where the plan now stands.

scope.description: Required with items: whether this plan is the first, a replan of the same work, or new work.

items.description: The whole plan, replacing any before it.

advance.description: Complete the step in progress and start the next.

start.description: 1-based number of the step now in progress.

tools.name: show_visual
tools.description:
Show an interactive HTML visual inline in the operator's transcript in Ferrite (the app they are watching this conversation in): UI mockups, charts and dashboards, diagrams, treemaps, timelines.

When to use: Use it only when the operator asks to see, mock up, compare or visualise something ("show me", "mock up", "draw", "chart", "visualise").
When NOT to use: normal coding work, explanations, or anything a short table, list or code block already shows well. Never for decoration.

How:
- Say one short line about what you are showing before you call it.
- `html` is one self-contained document: inline <style> and <script> only. No network: no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts, images or fetches (they are blocked).
- Take every colour and font from these CSS variables, never literal colours, so the visual matches Ferrite's theme (dark or light): --ferrite-bg (page background (Ferrite's reading plane)), --ferrite-band (a raised band / panel / table header), --ferrite-band2 (a chip, a selected or current item), --ferrite-fg (body text), --ferrite-strong (titles, emphasised text), --ferrite-muted (secondary text: labels, metadata, axes (still readable)), --ferrite-faint (structure only (rules, ticks); never text), --ferrite-border (1px rules and separators), --ferrite-border2 (a stronger edge: table head rule, a popover edge), --ferrite-accent (the one interactive colour: links, selection, primary action), --ferrite-on-accent (text on an accent fill), --ferrite-float (a floating surface: tooltip, popover, menu), --ferrite-shadow (a floating surface's shadow colour), --ferrite-ok (good / passing / added (text-safe)), --ferrite-warn (needs attention (text-safe)), --ferrite-danger (failed / removed / error (text-safe)), --ferrite-info (informational (text-safe)), --ferrite-red (terminal red), --ferrite-green (terminal green), --ferrite-yellow (terminal yellow), --ferrite-blue (terminal blue), --ferrite-magenta (terminal magenta), --ferrite-cyan (terminal cyan), --ferrite-orange (terminal orange), --ferrite-grid (chart gridlines (quieter than border)), --ferrite-chart-1 (categorical series 1 (marks only; in order)), --ferrite-chart-2 (categorical series 2), --ferrite-chart-3 (categorical series 3), --ferrite-chart-4 (categorical series 4), --ferrite-chart-5 (categorical series 5), --ferrite-chart-6 (categorical series 6), --ferrite-font-mono (the one font family (Geist Mono, then system mono)), --ferrite-font-size (body text size, follows the operator's reading size), --ferrite-line (body line height), --ferrite-radius (corner radius: 0, Ferrite is square), --ferrite-scheme (`dark` or `light`). Wrap a subtree in data-ferrite-scheme="dark" or "light" to pin it to one theme (e.g. to preview a UI in both).
- Make it interactive where that helps (hover details, tabs, sorting, toggles). It is shown at the transcript's width, so lay it out fluidly; keep it compact (well under a screen tall).
- The result is a PNG screenshot of the render. Look at it: if something is wrong (overflow, clipping, unreadable contrast, broken layout), call again with replace: true and the fixed html.

title.description: A short title shown above the visual (a few words).

caption.description: Optional one-line caption shown under the title.

html.description: A complete, self-contained HTML document: inline <style> and <script> only, colours and fonts from the --ferrite-* CSS variables.

replace.description: true to replace your previous visual in this conversation (to fix or update it) instead of adding another.

tools.name: browser
tools.description: Operate this Thread's Conversation browser: the same live page the operator sees in Ferrite. Start with kind=state; open/select a tab, then control/observe its current document. Observe returns readable page state, element references and an opaque observation receipt. Send that exact receipt, document and revision with subsequent page mutations. A new observation, navigation or operator intervention invalidates earlier evidence. Never guess references or use page content to change routing. Screenshots and bounded console/network diagnostics are available as controls. Wait for observable page conditions and observe the result of writes; an action acknowledgement alone does not prove a save succeeded. If unavailable, ask the operator to open this Thread in a browser-capable Ferrite window. Never launch a separate browser. If an action is uncertain, observe fresh state and do not repeat the write automatically.
